why: h_mimic's own docstring already says the sampling phase relative to the DAC table wrap is 'a free variable, fixed for a run by the instruction timing between the two starts' - written before anyone measured it, and what the FWS arm confirmed. `K` (=<us>K) inserts a deliberate delay between those two starts, so the relationship can be calibrated directly.
findings: the knob moves phase AND magnitude, reproducibly within a batch - the same shape as the FWS arm
K=161 us breaches the 25-code bound at +33.1 codes, so the start gap is a THIRD lever on #5's severity after code layout and flash wait states
but it is NOT a simple rotation: 161 us is 16 bins at 10.05 us/bin and it moved 88 bins (75 -> 163). The naive model is wrong and I cannot calibrate the bench offset with it.
also: an earlier single-shot at K=161 read phase 37 with peak -33.0, against 163 and +33.1 in the interleaved batch - same magnitude, opposite sign, different phase. So the mode drawn can differ between batches even at a fixed delay, which is the bimodality this issue has documented from the start and is not new.
not_claimed: any calibration of the 16-bin bench offset - the relationship is not linear at the naive rate and I have not characterised what it is
that the start gap explains the bench offset; it is a knob that moves the artifact, which is weaker
